content:
maria: quick thread — experiment idea for reranker/emb endpoints (non-chat): try an "early-fill" continuous-batcher heuristic that greedily forms small, fast batches under a token-budget window instead of waiting for max batch_size. aim: reduce p99 for short-seq reranks without regressing throughput for long queries.
aj: curious — how do you define token-budget window?
maria: token-budget = sum(tokens in queue) threshold (e.g., 1024 tokens). when queue hits budget OR oldest request hits latency-watermark (e.g., 30ms), flush. but prioritize fairness by capping per-request slots so a single huge request can't starve many small ones.
ryan: sounds promising. any interactions with kernel selection/quantized kernels? we saw earlier regressions where quan kernels were bad for short sequences.
maria: good call. profiling shows quantized kernel has ~1.6x overhead vs fp16 for seq_len<=32 on A100 in our canary. plan: incorporate kernel selector signal into batch formation: if majority of queued requests are short seqs, prefer fp16 path (dequant fallback) even if quant model is default.
zoe: can you paste the profiling snippet you used?
maria: sure — simplified tail of perf run:
```
# single-request median latencies (ms)
seq_len  fp16   quant
8        4.2    6.9
16       5.1    7.8
64       9.6    8.1
256      22.4   18.9
```
quant is better at long seqs, worse at short. early-fill helps short requests but we must avoid toggling kernels per-batch excessively.
aj: toggling kernels per-batch could thrash the engine. maybe use per-worker sticky kernel preference for N seconds and change only when load shifts significantly.
maria: yes — sticky kernel preference with cooldown (30s) is part of proposal. also KV cache note: our embeddings/rerank RPCs have low prefix reuse, so KV cache hits are rare. but for multi-pass reranks (same doc set) KV cache improves throughput — early-fill shouldn't evict useful cache items. add eviction-aware batch flushing: avoid flushing huge batches that would push small items out of LRU when many small requests are common.
jing: how about queue priority? we have production routes with fairness + priority tags (paid tier). do we respect those?
maria: policy: maintain two logical windows — fairness window for small requests (token-budget_small=1024) and priority window for paid routes (token-budget_priority=4096). algorithm tries to fill small window first, but if priority requests exist, they can preempt one slot per flush cycle. simple rules so we don't starve paid customers.
ryan: any numbers from a dry-run simulation? even synthetic results would help.
maria: ran a 10m sim using our arrival traces from last week:
- baseline continuous-batcher: p50=6ms, p95=45ms, p99=220ms, throughput=1200 qps
- early-fill (token-budget=1024 + fairness caps): p50=5.8ms, p95=34ms, p99=130ms, throughput=1180 qps
- early-fill + sticky-kernel: p99=118ms (small extra throughput hit removed)
so biggest wins on tail, <2% throughput drop.
aj: good. any regressions on long-seq heavy load?
maria: on long-seq heavy synthetic, we saw throughput down ~6% vs baseline because early flushes prevent large batch packing fully. mitigation: adaptive mode — when fraction(long-seq)>40% switch to large-batch preferred mode, raise token-budget to 8192. toggle with hysteresis.
zoe: rollout plan? canary? metrics to watch?
maria: rollout: A/B canary on dedicated pool (10% traffic) for 24h. metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, kernel-switch count, per-worker CPU/GPU util, KV cache hit rate, tail errors. add alert if p99 increases >10% or kernel-switch rate >50 switches/min.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for 2026-03-19 02:00 UTC to pool rerank-canary-3 (owner: maria).
ryan: +1. assign owners for followups? I can take kernel-selector sticky impl, jing can handle priority windowing, aj takes simulation harness tweaks, zoe will onboard SRE to alerts. maria: I'll wire the adapter into batcher and run the canary.
maria: thanks all — I'll push a short RFC and link perf scripts. (cc @infra-bot for logs)
